cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles, has just seen a vision of the glory of the LORD, and he's facedown on the ground. Then the voice speaks. 'Son of man,' He says, 'stand up on your feet and I will speak to you.'

cards.question: As the voice speaks, the Spirit enters Ezekiel and sets him on his feet.

cards.text: Ezekiel's back on his feet, and the LORD gets RIGHT to it. No small talk. 'I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me.'

cards.question: The LORD says Israel has been rebelling against Him. For how long?

answers.text: Them and their fathers to this day
Just for the last few years

cards.text: He calls them obstinate and stubborn children, and Ezekiel's opening line is 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' No icebreaker. No joke about the traffic on the way in.

cards.question: Whether Israel listens or refuses to listen, what does the LORD say they will know?

answers.text: That a prophet has been among them
That the exile is ending soon

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Ezekiel not to be afraid, three times in one verse. Friend, when somebody tells me not to be afraid THREE times, that's when I start hopping my gold base toward the exit.

cards.question: The LORD promises Ezekiel that the people around him will be easy to live among.

cards.text: Not even close. Briers and thorns surround him, and he dwells among scorpions. That's the neighborhood.

cards.question: Even if Israel refuses to listen, the LORD tells Ezekiel to ___ His words to them anyway.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Ezekiel himself. 'Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house.'

cards.question: To show he's not like that rebellious house, what does the LORD tell Ezekiel to do?

answers.text: Open his mouth and eat what he's given
Tear his robe and sit in the dust
Go and wash in the River Kebar

cards.text: Eat WHAT, exactly? Ezekiel looks up and sees a hand reaching out to him, holding something.

cards.question: In the hand reaching out to Ezekiel, there's a ___.

cards.text: He unrolls it right in front of Ezekiel, and it's covered in writing.

cards.question: The writing on the scroll is only on the front.
Israel is a rebellious house. So what kind of words fill that scroll?

cards.text: Front and back, lamentation, mourning and woe, and the LORD just said eat what I give you. I once watched a baker eat raw dough straight off the spoon and thought THAT was brave.
The LORD is still holding out that scroll of woe. 'Son of man,' He says, 'eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.'

cards.question: The LORD told Ezekiel not to be rebellious. So when he's told to eat the scroll, what does Ezekiel do?

answers.text: Opens his mouth and is fed the scroll
Asks for time to think it over
Reads it aloud to the exiles first

cards.text: And this isn't a nibble, friend. 'Son of man,' He says, 'eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.'

cards.question: That scroll is full of lamentation, mourning and woe. How does it taste in Ezekiel's mouth?

cards.text: Then the LORD sends him to the house of Israel, and Ezekiel won't even need a translator. He's not being sent to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language. No pointing, no nodding, no saying it LOUDER and SLOWER.

cards.question: The LORD says if He had sent Ezekiel to peoples whose language he couldn't understand, they would have listened to him.

cards.text: True, and that one stings. People who can't understand a word he says would listen, but the LORD says the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to him.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say the house of Israel won't listen to Ezekiel?

answers.text: Because they won't listen to the LORD
Because Ezekiel is a stranger to them
Because they can't understand his words

cards.text: The LORD says the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted. So He's got a plan for Ezekiel's face.

cards.question: The LORD says He will make Ezekiel's face as ___ as their faces.
The LORD says He will make Ezekiel's forehead like a diamond, harder than flint.

cards.text: Harder than flint, friend, while MY edges were going soft in the back of a junk drawer. Then the LORD adds, 'listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart.'

cards.question: Out of the whole house of Israel, which people does the LORD send Ezekiel to speak to?

answers.text: The king of Babylon and his court

cards.text: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up, and behind him comes a great rumbling sound: 'Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!'

cards.question: The rumbling comes from the wings of the living creatures brushing together and the ___ beside them.

cards.text: Wings and wheels, the same living creatures from his vision. Then the Spirit takes Ezekiel away, with the strong hand of the LORD upon him.

cards.question: As the Spirit carries him off, how does Ezekiel go?

answers.text: In bitterness and anger of spirit

cards.text: He comes to the exiles at Tel-abib, who live by the River Kebar. And the man with the diamond forehead doesn't say a word. He sits right where they sit.

cards.question: Ezekiel stays there among the exiles, overwhelmed, for ___ days.

cards.text: Seven days, overwhelmed, sitting right where they sit. And that's where we'll leave him for now, friend, because the LORD isn't finished with Ezekiel yet.

findings.problem: The opening card uses facts from outside the passage: Ezekiel is a priest among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1, 1:3), he has seen a vision of the glory of the LORD, and he fell facedown (Ezekiel 1:28). None of them has a reference. The card cites only Ezekiel 2:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it has 3 sentences: "Ezekiel's back on his feet..." / "No small talk." / the quote.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer "Them and their fathers to this day" names who and how long, with Bible-sounding wording. Both wrong answers give only a time span ("Only since the exile began", "Just for the last few years"). The right answer stands out as a different kind of answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "He calls them obstinate..." / "No icebreaker." / "No joke about the traffic on the way in."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 2:6 says "though briers and thorns surround you, and you dwell among scorpions." The card drops "though" and states it as plain fact: "Briers and thorns surround him, and he dwells among scorpions. That's the neighborhood."
This story card has 3 sentences: "Not even close." / "Briers and thorns surround him..." / "That's the neighborhood."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "To show he's not like that rebellious house" adds a purpose to the command to eat. Ezekiel 2:8 puts the two commands side by side but never says how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "It's covered in writing" suggests writing over the whole scroll. That gives away card 16, which asks whether the writing is only on the front.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Israel is a rebellious house. So what kind of words fill that scroll?" says the scroll holds woe because Israel is rebellious. Ezekiel 2:10 doesn't say why the scroll says what it says.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This card recaps Ezekiel 2:8-10 ("Front and back, lamentation, mourning and woe, and the LORD just said eat what I give you"), which cards 11-17 already told and asked. It doesn't move the passage forward.

"The LORD told Ezekiel not to be rebellious. So when he's told to eat the scroll..." gives Ezekiel a reason for obeying. Ezekiel 3:2 only says "So I opened my mouth" after the command in 3:1. It doesn't tie his obedience to the warning in 2:8.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "Then the LORD sends him..." / "He's not being sent..." / "No pointing, no nodding..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "MY edges were going soft in the back of a junk drawer" changes the backstory. His edges went soft on the Millers' counter, and that is why he was put in the drawer. The backstory never says they went soft in the drawer.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "The same living creatures from his vision" is a fact from Ezekiel 1 (for example 1:5, 1:15). It has no reference. The card cites only Ezekiel 3:13-14.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "The man with the diamond forehead" drops "like". Ezekiel 3:9 says "I will make your forehead like a diamond."
"Doesn't say a word" adds something Ezekiel 3:15 doesn't state. The verse says only that he sat where they sat and stayed among them, overwhelmed.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "He comes to the exiles..." / "And the man with the diamond forehead doesn't say a word." / "He sits right where they sit."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The last card opens by recapping what cards 18-19 already covered ("Seven days, overwhelmed, sitting right where they sit"). Since 3:15 was asked on a choice card, this card can be just the line saying the story isn't over.
Multiple choice takes 5 of the 10 choice cards in stop 2, against 2 true or false and 3 fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
